title: B3: cribl-decision B1 trained further on real-report sentences (AnnoCTR)
question: Does training on sentences from real vendor reports close the gap seen on CTI-HAL? Under the never-abstain rule B1 beat pipeline rank-1 by +0.10 on dev, +0.06 on public test and only +0.05 on CTI-HAL, and stayed below Jev C1 there.
harness: scripts/cribl_finetune/ (prepare_annoctr.py, export_cases.py --splits annoctr_*, train.py continued-arm options, evaluate.py, rescore.py); pod script scripts/cribl_finetune/runpod/remote_b3.sh

data.source: AnnoCTR (Lange et al., LREC-COLING 2024), github.com/boschresearch/anno-ctr-lrec-coling-2024 at d510b6949e1938d47c93a43eedd562dc538439dc, CC-BY-SA 4.0: 400 vendor reports (Intel471, Lab52, S2 Grupo, Proofpoint, QuoIntelligence, Zscaler); the 112 with ATT&CK technique links are used
data.cases: one case per sentence with at least one technique link (linking_mitre_only), gold = its linked techniques remapped to ATT&CK 19.2; AnnoCTR's own document split: train 1,884, dev 443, test 959 scorable sentences
data.labels: parent level: 0.5% of train sentences carry a sub-technique, against 45% of CTI-HAL statements; two thirds of the links are implicit mentions
data.candidates: the pipeline's top-10 (benchmark_mapping.py hybrid, exemplar index on: it holds only public train sentences), as for dev, test and CTI-HAL
data.overlap: no CTI-HAL statement of 8+ tokens occurs verbatim in any AnnoCTR report; AnnoCTR train drops exact and near (token Jaccard >= 0.9) duplicates of public dev/test, CTI-HAL and AnnoCTR dev/test texts
data.replay: 1,772 AnnoCTR train rows remain after the overlap filter (42 held-out duplicates, 70 repeats); an equal number of public train rows (cases_train.jsonl), a seeded sample, with the original exact targets, against forgetting

fixed.targets: AnnoCTR rows: common.family_target_distribution (uniform over offered options in a gold parent's family, or a gold sub-technique; none_of_these when none is offered); replay rows: common.target_distribution
fixed.training: QLoRA as B1/B2 (4-bit NF4, same LoRA modules, chat format, fp32 readout), lr 5e-5 (continued training; not tuned), cosine with 3% warmup, effective batch 16, 2 epochs, checkpoints every half epoch, seed 7
fixed.decision_rule: never_abstain (amendment 4 of the parent): the most probable of the ten techniques; P(none_of_these) is a flag
fixed.compute: RunPod secure RTX 4090; CTI-HAL uploaded for the scoring run with the owner's permission (2026-10-13) and deleted with the pod

selection.checkpoint: the B3 checkpoint with the highest AnnoCTR dev parent-aware score under never_abstain (AnnoCTR labels are parent level); ties the earlier
selection.reported_not_used: B1 and pipeline rank-1 on AnnoCTR dev

confirmation.runs: the selected B3 once on CTI-HAL (968), AnnoCTR test (959) and public test (1,391); B1 once on AnnoCTR test; everything rescored with rescore.py under never_abstain
confirmation.no_retuning: nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result

success.headline: CTI-HAL exact under never_abstain: B3 minus B1 (same rows, B1 from docs 21.3.18) with a paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
secondary: AnnoCTR test parent-aware under never_abstain: B3 minus B1, paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
CTI-HAL exact at least Jev C1 as reported (0.460)
public test exact: B3 minus B1 not below -0.02 (point estimate; forgetting check)

stop_rules: AnnoCTR train gold-family-in-candidates above 0.95 (a leak into the candidates): stop and inspect
more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
adoption: none: an experiment, no product wiring
reporting: every checkpoint's AnnoCTR dev curve (both rules), exact and parent-aware on every set, B1 vs B3 vs pipeline rank-1 vs Jev C1 (CTI-HAL), the none_of_these flag AUROC, explicit vs implicit AnnoCTR mentions, training time and cost
informed_by: the parent study's dev, public test and CTI-HAL results (docs 21.3.18) and AnnoCTR's statistics and dev candidate lists (gold family in the top 10 for 0.722 of dev sentences, exact id 0.436); no model has been scored on AnnoCTR

amendments.before: any B3 training or AnnoCTR scoring
amendments.change: compute is a RunPod secure A40 (48 GB, Ampere, EU-SE-1, $0.59/h) instead of an RTX 4090
amendments.reason: no secure RTX 4090 or L40 was available
amendments.deviation: a different GPU gives floating-point differences against B1's CTI-HAL and public test rows (scored on RTX 4090 pods); same code, seeds and data order
amendments.informed_by: nothing from B3 or AnnoCTR model scores (none exist)
